lemma: L-b1 (exact F_2 encoding of one THR gate). Let w in {0..W}^n, B = bitlength(W), K = sum_i popcount(w_i) <= nB, and t an integer. There is a system over F_2 in x_1..x_n plus aux variables with (i) every aux variable defined by one triangular equation of degree <= 2 with <= 4 monomials; (ii) the aux values are determined uniquely by x; (iii) the output bit equals [w.x >= t] for every x; (iv) number of adder aux variables A_add = 2(F+H) <= 2K + 2B + 2*ceil(log2 n), where F = full adders and H = half adders. Comparator aux: one per bit of the sum, L <= B + ceil(log2 n) + 1.
gap: Part (b) of Q-5339f27dd5. L-b1 gives an encoding with O(n log W) equations per bottom gate, so a THR o THR circuit with m bottom gates needs about m n log W equations. This is not <= c n equations once m log W is unbounded. Open: whether another encoding (shared equations across gates, or a different algebraic model) reaches <= c n equations. The counting theorem itself stays unverified (K7 Stage A blocked, primary source HTTP 403).
proved_step: PROOF (CLAIMED). (i),(ii): full adder on bits a,b,c of column j gives s = a+b+c mod 2 (linear eq s+a+b+c=0) and carry cy = maj(a,b,c) (eq cy+ab+bc+ca=0); half adder gives s = a+b (linear) and cy = ab (one monomial). Equations are ordered by creation, so each new variable is a function of earlier ones. (iii): over Z, a+b+c = s + 2cy (resp. a+b = s + 2cy), so each step preserves sum_j 2^j * (bits in column j) = w.x. Columns are processed low to high until each holds <= 1 bit; the final bits then encode w.x exactly, and the comparator recurrence G_{j+1} = (s_j OR G_j) if t_j = 0, (s_j AND G_j) if t_j = 1, with G_0 = 1, computes [S >= t] by induction on bits from LSB. (iv): each full adder lowers the total bit count by 1 and the count starts at K, so F <= K. Within one column the loop ends after at most one half adder, and carries only move upward, so H <= number of columns. The sum is at most nW < 2^(B + ceil(log2 n)), so there are at most B + ceil(log2 n) columns, giving H <= B + ceil(log2 n) and A_add = 2(F+H) <= 2K + 2B + 2 ceil(log2 n). Scope: the derivation is a proof by construction; the code cm-b569aea7a5a642ea (60 random instances, 293 solutions) and cm-0be807b33a714d1e are finite checks of the same gadgets (0 mismatches, max aux ratio 2.833 times n log W).

evidence: The construction uses standard full-adder and half-adder logic. Each full adder (s=a+b+c mod 2, cy=maj(a,b,c)) and half adder (s=a+b mod 2, cy=ab) are correctly mapped to F_2 equations of degree <= 2. The induction on bits for the comparator is a standard implementation of the magnitude comparison. The complexity bounds A_add <= 2K + 2B + 2 ceil(log2 n) follow directly from the ripple-carry structure where K is the sum of popcounts. Finite checks cm-b569aea7a5a642ea confirm 0 mismatches.

statement: For fixed W,k, a THR-of-THR circuit on n Boolean inputs with m bottom gates, bottom weights in {0,...,W}^n and at most k distinct bottom weight vectors has an exact uniquely extendible F_2 encoding of its bottom outputs using O_{W,k}(n) degree-2 equations, provided m<=n/log2(n+2). Boolean axioms are excluded.
proof: For each distinct weight vector build one L-b1 adder for its integer sum; bounded W gives O_W(n) equations. Reuse it across gates with that vector. Add one comparator per gate, using O_W(log(n+2)) equations; thresholds outside [1,sum_i w_i] are constants. Total is k O_W(n)+O_W(m log(n+2))=O_{W,k}(n). For comparison, process bits from most significant to least significant: initialize g=1, and at bit j replace g by (s_j OR g) if t_j=0, else (s_j AND g). Induction on the processed prefix gives g=[S>=t]. These are degree-2 equations over F_2 and uniquely define auxiliaries. Full-adder identities preserve the integer sum. This encodes bottom outputs only; top-gate encoding is outside scope.

statement: For L-bit integers S,T, scanning bits b_j,t_j from most significant to least, [S>=T] has an exact uniquely defined F_2 encoding with O(L) auxiliary variables and quadratic equations of at most four monomials each.
proof: Initialize e=1,g=0. At each bit introduce z=1+b+t, e'=e*z, u=e*b, v=u*(1+t), g'=g+v by equations defining each new variable. Expanding over F_2 gives degree at most 2 and at most four monomials per equation. Inductively e indicates equality of the scanned prefixes, and g indicates that the S prefix is strictly greater. z tests equality at this bit; v is 1 exactly when old prefixes were equal and b=1,t=0, the only event that first makes S greater. Thus the invariant is preserved. At the end g and e are mutually exclusive, so S>=T is their OR, encoded as h=g+e+g*e. All auxiliaries are uniquely determined in scan order. This repairs the comparator subclaim of S0003 but does not establish an O(n)-equation encoding for unrestricted THR o THR circuits.

statement: For fixed constants W,k, let a THR-of-THR circuit have m bottom gates on n Boolean inputs, all bottom weights in {0,...,W}^n, at most k distinct bottom weight vectors, and m<=n/log2(n+2). The vector of bottom outputs has an exact uniquely extendible encoding over F_2 with O_{W,k}(n) auxiliary variables and quadratic defining equations, each with at most four monomials. Boolean input axioms are excluded. This restricted construction does not claim to encode the top gate.
proof: For each distinct weight vector build one L-b1 adder for its integer sum; by L-b1 and fixed W its equations and auxiliaries number O_W(n). Reuse these sum bits for each gate with that vector. For each gate, thresholds outside the attainable interval yield a constant output. Otherwise the threshold uses O_W(log(n+2)) bits. Compare sum and threshold from most significant bit down, starting e=1,g=0; for current bits b,t set z=1+b+t, e'=ez, u=eb, v=u(1+t), g'=g+v over F_2, and output h=g+e+ge. Inductively e means equal prefixes and g means strictly greater prefixes; thus h=[S>=T]. Each auxiliary is uniquely defined in order, with degree at most two and at most four monomials per equation. The total is k O_W(n)+O_W(m log(n+2))=O_{W,k}(n). This proves the stated subclass only. Barrier diagnostic: this encoding construction is not a P-vs-NP lower-bound argument; no natural-proof, relativization, algebrization, or localization circumvention claim is made.

statement: For fixed constants W and r, any family of bottom threshold gates on n Boolean inputs with weights in {0,...,W}^n and at most r distinct (weight vector, threshold) pairs has an exact uniquely extendible F_2 encoding of all bottom outputs using O_{W,r}(n) quadratic defining equations with at most four monomials each. Boolean input axioms are excluded; the top gate is not encoded.
proof: For each distinct pair (w,t), build one exact threshold encoding using L-b1 for the weighted sum and the corrected MSB-first comparator from S0004: initialize e=1,g=0; on bits b,t' set z=1+b+t', e'=ez, u=eb, v=u(1+t'), g'=g+v, and output h=g+e+ge over F_2. The prefix invariant gives h=[w.x>=t]. Repeated gates with the same pair have exactly the same output function and reuse this entire encoding. There are at most r encodings, each with O_W(n) equations and auxiliaries, so the total is O_{W,r}(n). All auxiliary variables are defined in topological order, giving unique extension for each Boolean input. This is a restricted sharing result and does not close G0001 for unrestricted THR o THR circuits.
